Definition: from G4862 and G520; to take off together, i.e. transport with (seduce, passively, yield):--carry (lead) away with, condescend.
BiblicalUsage: Paul says the other Jews dissembled with Peter, insomuch that Barnabas also was carried away with their dissimulation. Even Barnabas, the son of consolation, can be swept along by a stronger current, and the verse is a warning that no one is too steady to be carried away.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that even good men can be carried away by bad company, and I hold that I must watch the current I am standing in before it sweeps me along.
